answer_text:
Here is a comprehensive guide to paying your **federal taxes online** through the IRS:

---

## 💻 How to Pay Federal Taxes Online

The IRS offers several convenient and secure ways to pay your federal taxes online. You can make a tax payment anytime online, from your bank account, with a card, or by mail.

---

### 1. 🏦 IRS Direct Pay (FREE – No Fees)
**Website:** [irs.gov/payments/direct-pay](https://www.irs.gov/payments/direct-pay-with-bank-account)

Pay personal or business taxes directly from your bank account with IRS Direct Pay. It's free and secure. You can pay balance due, federal tax deposits, and other federal income taxes. A single payment cannot exceed $10 million. To make a higher payment, use the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS) or same-day wire.

---

### 2. 👤 IRS Online Account (FREE – No Fees)
**Website:** [irs.gov/account](https://www.irs.gov/payments)

Sign in or create an account to pay now or schedule a payment. You can pay your tax balance due, estimated payments, or part of a payment plan. You can pay now or schedule payments up to a year in advance.

---

### 3. 🏛️ Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS)
**Website:** [eftps.gov](https://www.eftps.gov)

Set up the Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS) for individual or business tax payments. Note that new EFTPS accounts can take up to five business days to process. This is ideal for larger payments and recurring scheduled payments.

---

### 4. 💳 Debit/Credit Card or Digital Wallet (Fees Apply)
**Website:** [irs.gov/payments/pay-taxes-by-debit-or-credit-card](https://www.irs.gov/payments/pay-your-taxes-by-debit-or-credit-card)

You can pay online or over the phone, and you can pay using digital wallets such as PayPal and Click to Pay. Processing fees apply, and there's a maximum number of card payments allowed based on your tax type and payment type.

---

### 5. 📱 IRS2Go Mobile App
Use the IRS2Go mobile app for easy and secure mobile payments. The app is available for both iOS and Android.

---

### 📅 Important Deadlines & Tips

- Payment for taxes you owe is due by the filing deadline even if you get a filing extension. The filing deadline for 2025 tax returns was April 15, 2026.
- The IRS encourages you to pay your taxes in full because penalties and interest will continue to grow until you pay the full balance.
- Individuals, including sole proprietors, partners, and S corporation shareholders, generally have to make estimated tax payments if they expect to owe tax of $1,000 or more when their return is filed.

---

### 💡 Can't Pay in Full?

You can find details on payment plan types including simple, streamlined, in-business trust fund express, guaranteed, and partial payment installment agreements. You can also check if you can settle your debt for less than you owe with an Offer in Compromise.
